notes:
Summary: enterprise evaluation for Private VPC deployment focusing on compliance mapping (SOC 2, ISO27001, HIPAA/BAA, PCI). Company runs a hybrid payments + patient-intake platform; strict EU/US residency and audit trail requirements. CTO quote: "We cannot have PHI leave our VPC or be logged in a non-audited store."

Recent timeline:
- 2026-02-12: Intro demo (ff recording: FF-2026-02-12-ceres-demo). Discussed Redwood private control plane, VPC peering, KMS options. AE (Maya) + SE (Ravi) on call.
- 2026-02-20: Security questionnaire submitted (attached drive/security/ceres_shield_security_faq_v1.md).
- 2026-02-26: Legal requested BAA draft and PCI scoping note.
- 2026-03-01: Architecture sync; customer provided network diagram and legacy DB list.
- 2026-03-08: Follow-up on KMS integration and encryption-at-rest responsibilities.

Compliance mapping (high level):
- SOC 2: Redwood private deployment + VPC isolation addresses CC6/CC7 network security and logical access controls. Audit logging and per-request traces map to CC3 and CC5 (change management + monitoring). SE to provide logging retention options and sample audit log export.
- ISO 27001: Customer wants evidence for A.10 (cryptography) and A.12 (operations). KMS integration and HSM-backed key wrap recommended; request for Redwood to produce control mappings and SOC2 report.
- HIPAA / BAA: Ceres Shield processes PHI in some workflows (intake forms + payment metadata). BAA required before POC. Requirements: encryption in transit + at rest, dedicated logging, breach notification SLA, restricted access lists. Customer asked to see data flow showing PHI never leaves their VPC-managed subnet.
- PCI considerations: Cardholder data (CHD) will be kept out of Redwood store where possible; tokenization recommended. Customer wants PCI scope reduction guidance and confirmation that Redwood will not retain PANs in logs. Need PCI scoping note from Security.

Technical asks & Redwood fit: 
- VPC deployment: need private control plane with optional customer-managed endpoints. Customer requires VPC peering or PrivateLink per region (EU + US).
- KMS: must support customer-managed keys (CMK) with HSM, rotate keys quarterly, and allow for key revocation audit.
- Audit logging: immutable, exportable logs (S3/GCS) with retention policy configurable to 7+ years. Audit events must include token-level invocation metadata, model version, route, and user id.
- Data residency: per-tenant data partitioning and region pinning; POC must run in EU for EU customers, US in US.
- Fallbacks/routing: offline fallback to smaller quantized model in case of capacity/latency issues. Customer asked about deterministic routing policy and retention differences by tier.

POC plan (proposed):
1) Week 0: NDA + BAA counter-sign (legal).
2) Week 1: Provide VPC reference architecture + KMS integration doc (SE).
3) Week 2: Stand up POC in customer EU region (private control plane), connect to CMK, enable audit logging to their S3.
4) Week 3: Run 2 sample workloads (support-agent + payments tokenization) and capture audit logs for compliance review.
5) Week 4: Security review call, deliver SOC2 report and ISO mapping artifact.

Open questions / action items (short):
- SE (Ravi) to create KMS keyflow diagram and clarify who performs key rotation; provide example IAM policies.
- AE (Maya) to escalate BAA to contracts; request expected legal turnaround.
- Customer to provide list of systems that store CHD/PHI to finalize PCI/HIPAA scope.
- Security to confirm log retention SLA and sample export format (csv/json).

Staging notes (tone): choppy CRM-style fragments common in account notes. Customer is risk-averse but budgeted for private deployment if compliance gates clear. Decision makers: CTO (L. Moreno), Head of Security (A. Patel), Procurement lead (S. Byrne).
